projects.title: Warp and Weft
projects.summary: A real-time WebGPU meadow cut into a checker, with one white chair as the only object.
projects.description: A field of grass blades is mown into a checker and one plastic chair stands on a dark square. 265,744 blades bend in the wind in real time, and the pointer parts them. Built in WebGPU with a film pass for halation, grain, and vignette.

caseStudy.brief: A WebGPU field of grass had to read as cloth. The scene needed one object, one checker cut, and no visible blade cards. The page had to run in a browser tab at full desktop width, hold a steady frame, and keep the chair readable at phone width. The field is the subject, and the chair is the scale reference.
process: A clump table and blade generators build the meadow. Each clump shares a colour field, so the checker reads at distance without a texture.
A vertex shader bends the blades in the wind. The wind runs on a slow noise field, and a pointer ray parts the grass around the cursor.
A mask cuts the field into a checker. The dark squares use a shorter blade and a cooler colour, so the pattern survives the camera move.
One GLB chair sits on a dark square. The chair is the only hard edge in the frame, and it gives the field a human scale.
A film pass adds halation, grain, and vignette. The grade stays low-contrast so the white chair holds against the grass.
The camera keeps a low eye height. The horizon stays out of frame, so the field reads as cloth rather than a landscape.
The drawing buffer caps at the viewport size. The blade count is fixed when the scene starts, so the meadow holds 60 fps on a laptop and on a phone.
A small status line reports frame rate and blade count. The test run read 265,744 blades at 60 fps.
The GLB chair loads once and is drawn once. The meadow uses no textures; colour comes from the clump fields.
result: 60 fps at 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844 in headless Chrome 156.
Chrome reports no console errors at both widths.

projects.title: Viscous Orb
projects.summary: A fluid orb with a living dye trail, spectral rim, and a moving dither veil.
projects.description: A single glowing sphere holds a real-time fluid surface. Pointer motion and an invisible mover push velocity and dye through the field, and the surface settles after each pass. The veil turns the moving liquid into coarse Bayer pixels. The rim stays analytic, and no tiled texture is sampled in the reflection.

caseStudy.brief: A single sphere had to hold a real-time fluid interior and keep a clean silhouette. The earlier build used a tiled caustic texture, and the grid repeated in the reflection. The target was a liquid surface that reacts to a pointer, settles on its own, and holds 60 fps at portrait size. The page also had to run inside a portfolio iframe with a capped drawing buffer.
process: The study renders one sphere and one full-screen fluid pass. A pointer ray hits the sphere, and the hit point writes velocity and dye into a 256 x 256 field. An invisible mover crosses the orb on a loop, so the surface moves without input.
A pressure solve and a vorticity pass move the dye through the field. The velocity decays after each pass. The dye carries the colour, and the field returns to rest in about one second.
The first build sampled a tiled caustic texture. The tiles showed as a grid in the reflection. I removed the texture and drove the reflection from the fluid field. The grid artifact disappeared.
A Bayer veil reads the dye and turns the moving liquid into coarse pixels. The veil clears as the field settles. A toggle keeps the veil off for clean stills.
Bloom runs at quarter resolution with two blur passes. Soft focus mixes the blurred frame at 0.42. An analytic rim keeps the silhouette sharp while the interior stays soft.
The portfolio embed sets a 1728 px drawing buffer cap. The study scales the fluid field and the bloom pass to that cap, so the frame rate holds at desktop and phone width.
result: 59.7 fps at 1440 x 900 and 59.4 fps at 390 x 844 in headless Chrome 156.
The portfolio embed caps the drawing buffer at 1728 px.
Chrome reports no console errors at desktop and phone width.
The still shows the dither veil and the spectral rim. The touch frame shows the dye trail.

projects.title: Motion
projects.summary: Personal experiments in motion graphics, abstract form, and procedural animation.
projects.description: A collection of personal experiments and studies in motion graphics, focused on exploring visual dynamics, abstract forms, and procedural animation techniques. These pieces were created as personal challenges to push the boundaries of my skills and test new concepts.
projects.tools: Adobe After Effects, Adobe Photoshop, and Blender

projects.title: Forget Me Not Exhibition
projects.summary: Projection mapping and technical integration for an immersive light and video installation.
projects.description: Provided technical setup and specialized support for this immersive light and video installation by Victoria. My role was projection mapping and technical integration. I was responsible for fitting the artist's video content onto the complex surfaces of the exhibition space, including the bed, walls, and sink.
projects.tools: Resolume and MadMapper calibration and programming, on-site technical setup, and light/loop playback management

projects.title: 9ine5ive6eis
projects.summary: Visual identity, cloud graphic, custom typography, and a motion loop for a limited apparel release.
projects.description: This project was an assignment to create the visual identity for a specific release within an ongoing apparel series. My contribution centered on the creation of the cloud graphic and custom typography, which was produced for a limited run on t-shirts and tote bags. I also created the accompanying brand motion graphic loop. This was a collaborative effort, with my work integrating into the final product photography provided by other artists.

projects.title: Triqueta AR/VR Exhibition
projects.summary: AR overlays and a VR experience built around Michael Flanagan's paintings and video works.
projects.description: Triqueta was a collaborative exhibition project developed for the McAllen Creative Incubator. The project allowed me to develop and experiment with Augmented Reality and Virtual Reality, integrating them with the established artistic practice of filmmaker and artist Michael Flanagan. I focused on the technical development, creating a unique VR experience that incorporated Flanagan's video works, and building AR overlays for his original paintings, which also featured AI-generated elements. This installation explored the intersection of traditional painting, AI, and new media.
projects.tools: VR (Unreal), AR, and AI-assisted art. Collaborator: Michael Flanagan.

projects.title: Tigers Blood
projects.summary: A commissioned 3D animation of a static 2D logo, finished with metallic textures and analog video effects.
projects.description: Commissioned to create a dynamic digital asset from the client's static 2D logo. The process involved converting the original artwork into a 3D model, then applying a distinct lo-fi chromotype aesthetic with metallic textures and analog video effects. The final animation uses keyframed movement and a subtle glitch/vibration to transform the identity into a bold promotional graphic.
projects.tools: 3D modeling, texturing, lighting, animation, and compositing

projects.title: River Pierce Foundation AR Showcase
projects.summary: Commissioned augmented reality project for River Pierce Foundation's 2025 event program.
projects.description: A commissioned augmented reality project debuted alongside The Teaching of the Hands experimental documentary screening and panel discussion at Treviño–Uribe Rancho in San Ygnacio, Texas.
